rationale: Start with a broad, strong scouting gradient at mid temperature to maximize the chance that all 10 compounds elute within 42 min while giving enough gradient time to reveal where the crowded regions are. This first run should map the overall retention window and show whether later optimization should focus on shortening, narrowing, or shifting the gradient.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is to reduce analysis time. Keep the same wide gradient and temperature but shorten tG one step to test how much faster we can go before any pair drops below the 1.5 resolution threshold.

The 16 min gradient is still fully resolved and only barely penalized on time, so shorten the gradient again to try to bring the last peak under 10 min. The critical pair is already the same crowded region, so this directly probes whether 14 min is still above the resolution limit.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, so now target the single weak pair by making the gradient slightly less steep without lengthening it. Lowering phi1 should selectively spread the later part of the chromatogram and may recover pair 6/7 above 1.5 while keeping t_last under 10 min.

The lower phi1 improved the critical 6/7 pair while keeping the last peak under 10 min, so continue in the same direction one more step. This should further shallow the effective gradient around the crowded mid-late region and may push the last unresolved pair to full credit without incurring a time penalty.

The best point so far is close to ideal: 14 min, phi1 0.90 gives only one slightly under-resolved pair but no time penalty. A small increase in temperature may speed the run just enough to keep t_last safely below 10 min while preserving or modestly improving selectivity around the critical 6/7 pair.

Temperature clearly harms the key selectivity, so return to 40 C. Since phi1 0.85 restored full resolution but was only slightly too slow, shorten tG to 12 min to try to pull the last peak back under 10 min while keeping the favorable selectivity of the lower phi1 setting.

The critical 6/7 pair is the only limiter, and higher temperature strongly worsened it, so test the opposite direction. A slightly cooler run with a modestly longer gradient than the current best should improve selectivity enough to reach full resolution while likely keeping the last peak near the 10 min target.

Changing temperature was unfavorable, so probe a composition shift instead: raise phi0 one step while keeping the current best tG and phi1. This should reshape the early-to-mid gradient profile and may open the crowded central cluster around the critical pair without pushing the last peak past 10 min.

The phi0 increase improved the critical pair while keeping the run comfortably under 10 min, so now combine that gain with a slightly lower phi1 to further flatten the gradient in the crowded region. This is a direct shot at pushing pair 6/7 to full resolution while still staying near the time optimum.

You have reached full score, so the only remaining useful exploration is to find whether an even shorter method can still preserve full resolution. Shortening tG by one step from the current optimum directly tests whether the critical 6/7 pair can stay at or above 1.5 while pulling the last peak clearly below 10 min.

Since 12 min was too steep, stay at 14 min and test whether one more decrease in phi1 can preserve full resolution with a more comfortable margin while checking if the time remains acceptable. This helps define the robustness boundary around the current optimum without leaving the high-performing region.

The optimum is likely on a narrow ridge near the current method, so test a further increase in phi0 while keeping the proven phi1 and tG. This may preserve the strong 6/7 resolution while shaving a little late retention, potentially giving a more robust full-score method with t_last just under 10 min.

The higher phi0 improved the full-score method by moving t_last farther below 10 min while keeping all pairs resolved, so continue one more step in that direction. This tests whether the same selectivity can be retained with an even faster, more comfortable full-resolution window.

Phi0 0.15 appears to be on the full-score ridge and gives more resolution margin than 0.10, so it is the best candidate for a shorter method. Reducing tG to 12 min tests whether that extra margin is enough to keep the critical 6/7 pair at full credit while gaining additional speed.

At phi0 0.15 and tG 14 min, the method has full score with some margin on the critical pair, so now test whether a slightly higher phi1 can reduce t_last further without losing full resolution. This explores whether the true fastest full-score point lies just above the current optimum in phi1.

A 12 min gradient needs more selectivity around pair 6/7, and lowering phi1 previously increased that margin. Combining phi0 0.15 with phi1 0.80 at 12 min is the most plausible remaining shot at achieving full resolution in a shorter method than the current 14 min optimum.

With the composition space largely mapped, the remaining question is whether a small temperature decrease can lift the marginal 1.61 pair enough to support later speed-ups without shifting to the bad selectivity regime seen at 35 C for a different composition. Testing the current full-score composition at 35 C checks that local temperature effect directly.

Temperature has proven detrimental, so use the remaining runs to finish composition-slope mapping around the 12 min boundary. Phi0 0.10 with lower phi1 gave the highest resolution margin at 14 min, making it the best remaining candidate to rescue full resolution at 12 min.

The remaining useful gap is whether the full-score ridge at phi0 0.15 can be shifted to lower phi1 without losing score. This run checks if a lower phi1 at the stronger phi0 still maintains full resolution and perhaps offers a more robust alternative to the current best methods.

With only a few injections left and full score already achieved, the best use is to bracket the upper phi1 edge around the phi0 0.15 optimum. This tests whether a steeper end composition can still preserve full resolution while offering a potentially faster or more robust full-score alternative.
